newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE 100 seen rising after consolidation.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE 100 seen rising after consolidation.

text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index continued in its consolidation phase on Thursday, stuck within its trading range of the past six sessions, yet chart analysts said the index looked well placed to break through to higher ground.

Richard Marshall at Investment Research of Cambridge said the persistent strength of gilts should continue to support shares, even as Wall Street succumbs to profit-taking after its recent surge to a succession of record highs.
"The FTSE is in a consolidation phase and I don't really trust it," Marshall said, "but with gilts powering ahead that is normally very healthy for equities."

Marshall said the a close above 4,070 on the FTSE in healthy volume could be a signal for a fresh move upwards in the UK index, which has lately been consolidating since it reached an intraday record of 4,094.4 on November 26.
"The short-term trading pattern on the FTSE could turn into a bullish "flag" pattern but first a close over 4,070 is required, accompanied by high volume," Marshall said.
He also pointed out that the advance/decline indicator on the FTSE rose on Wednesday, the first time this had happened since the first week of October, despite the index's 16.3-point decline.
Sharon Quinn at MMS International also said the FTSE was well placed to challenge its recent record highs, though it would meet strong resistance at 4,100.
"At the moment we are in a consolidation phase," Quinn said, "but the index is looking pretty good as long as it holds above trend line support at 4,033."
By 1138 GMT the FTSE was up 30.2 points at 4,075.4. The long gilt future was up 5.32 at 111-9/16.
